UMF grew out of TableSpec's table schemas. The next step is to bring that tooling onto the shared model, then use it in graph systems.

Pack schemas document a domain. Data generation and loading belong to their consuming tools.

Available

TableSpec

Table schemas and pipeline tooling

A Python library for schema validation, profiling, SQL and PySpark schema generation, and documentation. It uses the earlier table-oriented UMF format; the move to this library's shared model is planned.

GitHub ↗Documentation ↗
Published site

Weft

UMF-powered SQL compiler

Write queries against supplied UMF models and compile SQL for Truss on PostgreSQL or Ashlar on Databricks. Weft returns parameters, result types, decoding instructions and diagnostics; the host executes the query.

Compiler support is qualified for specific versions and fixture profiles. Packages are not yet published, and production storage compatibility remains unqualified.

Website ↗GitHub ↗
Planned

Truss

Property graphs on SQL

A proposed graph engine, starting on PostgreSQL, that would use UMF schemas to type property values. It is still being designed; no engine has shipped.

GitHub ↗
Planned

Ashlar

Graphs on Databricks

A proposed graph data model for Databricks. The plan is to use UMF schemas for immutable graph revisions. The project is still being designed; no Databricks integration has shipped.
